# 3-Week Peaking Block for Powerlifting Meet

## Overview & Philosophy

Your client has completed 12 weeks of accumulation and enters this block with a solid base. The next 21 days will strip away fatigue while preserving strength and power. You'll reduce volume by ~40–50% week-on-week, maintain or slightly elevate intensity on the competition lifts, and strategically manage recovery to ensure she's neurologically fresh and physically recovered on meet day.

The three phases are:
- **Week 1 (Days 1–7):** Moderate taper; competition lift focus
- **Week 2 (Days 8–14):** Aggressive taper; intensity peaks
- **Week 3 (Days 15–21):** Deload + meet prep; technical work only

---

## Week 1: Moderate Taper & Competition Focus

**Training Days:** 4 sessions (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri)  
**Volume Reduction:** ~30% from accumulation phase  
**Intensity:** 85–92% 1RM on main lifts

### Session 1A – Squat Focus (Monday)

**Warm-up:**
- 5 min easy bike
- Bodyweight squats × 8
- Leg swings × 8 each direction
- Glute bridges × 10

**Main Work:**
- Squat: 2 × 2 @ 90% 1RM (rest 3 min)
- Squat: 1 × 1 @ 92% 1RM (rest 3 min)

**Accessory (reduced volume):**
- Paused squat (2-sec pause): 2 × 3 @ 80% 1RM (rest 2 min)
- Leg press: 2 × 5 @ RPE 7 (rest 90 sec)

**Finisher:**
- Sled push: 2 × 20m @ moderate load
- Hamstring curls: 2 × 8 @ RPE 7

**Duration:** ~50 minutes

---

### Session 1B – Bench Press Focus (Tuesday)

**Warm-up:**
- 5 min rowing machine
- Band pull-aparts × 15
- Incline push-ups × 8
- Scapular wall slides × 10

**Main Work:**
- Bench press: 2 × 2 @ 88% 1RM (rest 3 min)
- Bench press: 1 × 1 @ 91% 1RM (rest 3 min)

**Accessory:**
- Close-grip bench: 2 × 4 @ 85% 1RM (rest 2 min)
- Dumbbell floor press: 2 × 6 @ RPE 7 (rest 90 sec)

**Finisher:**
- Chest-supported row: 2 × 6 @ RPE 7
- Tricep dips (assisted if needed): 2 × 5 @ RPE 7

**Duration:** ~45 minutes

---

### Session 1C – Deadlift Focus (Thursday)

**Warm-up:**
- 5 min rowing
- Cat-cow stretches × 8
- Glute bridges × 10
- Inchworms × 8

**Main Work:**
- Deadlift: 2 × 2 @ 89% 1RM (rest 3 min)
- Deadlift: 1 × 1 @ 93% 1RM (rest 3 min)

**Accessory:**
- Deficit deadlift (2–3 inch): 2 × 3 @ 85% 1RM (rest 2 min)
- Trap bar deadlift: 2 × 4 @ RPE 7 (rest 2 min)

**Finisher:**
- Pendulum squat: 2 × 8 @ RPE 6
- Back extension: 2 × 8 @ RPE 6

**Duration:** ~50 minutes

---

### Session 1D – Upper Body Maintenance (Friday)

**Warm-up:**
- 5 min bike
- Band work × 15 reps (pull-aparts, face pulls, reverse flyes)

**Main Work:**
- Incline bench: 2 × 5 @ RPE 7 (rest 2 min)
- Barbell row: 2 × 5 @ RPE 7 (rest 2 min)

**Accessory:**
- Dumbbell bench: 2 × 6 @ RPE 6
- Seal rows: 2 × 8 @ RPE 6
- Lat pulldown: 2 × 8 @ RPE 6

**Finisher:**
- Pallof press: 2 × 8 each side @ light
- Dead bugs: 2 × 10

**Duration:** ~40 minutes

---

## Week 2: Aggressive Taper & Intensity Peak

**Training Days:** 3 sessions (Mon, Wed, Fri)  
**Volume Reduction:** ~50% from accumulation phase  
**Intensity:** 90–95% 1RM on main lifts

### Session 2A – Squat Peak (Monday)

**Warm-up:**
- 5 min easy bike
- Bodyweight squats × 8
- Leg swings × 8 each direction
- Glute bridges × 10

**Main Work:**
- Squat: 1 × 2 @ 91% 1RM (rest 3 min)
- Squat: 1 × 1 @ 94% 1RM (rest 3 min)
- Squat: 1 × 1 @ 95% 1RM (rest 4 min) — *This should feel strong but not maximal*

**Accessory (minimal):**
- Paused squat: 1 × 3 @ 80% 1RM (rest 2 min)
- Leg press: 1 × 5 @ RPE 6

**Duration:** ~40 minutes

---

### Session 2B – Bench Press Peak (Wednesday)

**Warm-up:**
- 5 min rowing
- Band pull-aparts × 15
- Incline push-ups × 8

**Main Work:**
- Bench press: 1 × 2 @ 89% 1RM (rest 3 min)
- Bench press: 1 × 1 @ 92% 1RM (rest 3 min)
- Bench press: 1 × 1 @ 94% 1RM (rest 4 min) — *Confident single, not a grinder*

**Accessory:**
- Close-grip bench: 1 × 4 @ 85% 1RM (rest 2 min)
- Dumbbell floor press: 1 × 5 @ RPE 6

**Duration:** ~35 minutes

---

### Session 2C – Deadlift Peak (Friday)

**Warm-up:**
- 5 min rowing
- Cat-cow stretches × 8
- Glute bridges × 10
- Inchworms × 8

**Main Work:**
- Deadlift: 1 × 2 @ 90% 1RM (rest 3 min)
- Deadlift: 1 × 1 @ 91% 1RM (rest 3 min)
- Deadlift: 1 × 1 @ 95% 1RM (rest 4 min) — *Strong, controlled rep*

**Accessory:**
- Deficit deadlift: 1 × 3 @ 85% 1RM (rest 2 min)
- Trap bar deadlift: 1 × 3 @ RPE 6

**Duration:** ~40 minutes

---

## Week 3: Deload & Meet Preparation

**Training Days:** 2 sessions (Mon, Wed)  
**Volume Reduction:** ~70% from accumulation phase  
**Intensity:** Technical work only; no heavy singles

This week prioritizes recovery, movement quality, and mental preparation. No maximal efforts.

### Session 3A – Squat & Bench Technique (Monday)

**Warm-up:**
- 8 min easy bike
- Bodyweight squats × 10
- Band work × 15 reps

**Main Work:**
- Squat: 3 × 2 @ 75% 1RM (rest 2 min) — *Focus on depth, speed, control*
- Bench press: 3 × 2 @ 75% 1RM (rest 2 min) — *Smooth, explosive reps*

**Accessory (light):**
- Leg press: 2 × 5 @ RPE 5
- Dumbbell bench: 2 × 5 @ RPE 5

**Finisher:**
- Mobility work: 10 min (hip flexor stretch, thoracic rotation, shoulder dislocates)

**Duration:** ~45 minutes

---

### Session 3B – Deadlift Technique (Wednesday)

**Warm-up:**
- 8 min easy rowing
- Cat-cow stretches × 10
- Glute bridges × 10
- Inchworms × 8

**Main Work:**
- Deadlift: 3 × 2 @ 75% 1RM (rest 2 min) — *Perfect setup, smooth pull, controlled descent*

**Accessory (light):**
- Trap bar deadlift: 2 × 3 @ RPE 5
- Back extension: 2 × 5 @ RPE 5

**Finisher:**
- Mobility work: 10 min (hamstring stretch, spinal flexion/extension, glute activation)

**Duration:** ~40 minutes

---

## Meet Day (Friday of Week 3)

**No training.** Light warm-up 2–3 hours before competition:
- 10 min easy cardio
- Dynamic stretches
- 2–3 empty bar reps of each lift
- Mental visualization

---

## Nutrition & Recovery Recommendations

### Caloric Intake
- **Weeks 1–2:** Maintain accumulation-phase calories (no aggressive deficit). Slight surplus is acceptable to support recovery.
- **Week 3:** Maintain calories; do not cut aggressively. Adequate fuel supports nervous system recovery.

### Macronutrients
- **Protein:** 0.8–1.0 g per lb bodyweight daily (supports muscle retention during taper)
- **Carbs:** Front-load around training sessions; reduce slightly in Week 3 as volume drops
- **Fats:** Maintain 0.3–0.4 g per lb for hormone support

### Hydration & Electrolytes
- 3–4 liters water daily
- Sodium intake slightly elevated (supports water retention and CNS function)

### Sleep & Recovery
- **Target:** 8–9 hours nightly
- **Week 3:** Prioritize sleep above all else; consider an extra 30–60 min if possible
- Avoid new stressors; manage work/life stress actively

### Supplementation (Optional)
- Creatine monohydrate: 5 g daily (if already taking; continue)
- Caffeine: Moderate intake; avoid excessive use in Week 3 to preserve sleep
- Magnesium glycinate: 300–400 mg before bed (supports sleep quality)

### Meal Timing Around Training
- **2–3 hours pre-training:** Balanced meal (carbs + protein + minimal fat)
- **Within 30 min post-training:** Protein + carbs (e.g., whey shake + banana, or chicken + rice)

---

## Monitoring & Adjustments

### Red Flags (Reduce Intensity if Present)
- Persistent soreness or joint pain
- Sleep disruption or excessive fatigue
- Elevated resting heart rate (>10 bpm above baseline)
- Loss of appetite or mood changes

### Green Lights (Proceed as Planned)
- Lifts feel fast and crisp
- Normal sleep and appetite
- Confidence and excitement building
- No pain, only normal muscle soreness

### If Adjustments Needed
- **Feeling flat in Week 2?** Add 1–2 extra rest days; reduce intensity by 2–3%.
- **Feeling strong?** Proceed as written; do not add volume.
- **Minor aches?** Increase mobility work; reduce accessory volume further.

---

## Summary Table

| **Week** | **Sessions** | **Main Lift Volume** | **Intensity** | **Focus** |
|----------|-------------|----------------------|---------------|-----------|
| 1        | 4           | 3–4 reps per lift    | 85–92%        | Competition lift focus; moderate taper |
| 2        | 3           | 2–3 reps per lift    | 90–95%        | Intensity peak; aggressive taper |
| 3        | 2           | 2 reps per lift      | 75% (technical) | Deload; recovery; meet prep |

---

## Final Notes

This block is designed to strip fatigue while maintaining strength and power. Your client should feel **fresher and faster** by meet day, not weaker. The key is discipline: resist the urge to add volume or test maxes in Week 3. Trust the process.

On meet day, she'll open conservatively (85–87%), move to a confident second attempt (90–92%), and attempt a meet PR on the third. The taper will have her feeling strong, fast, and ready.

Good luck to your client at the meet!
